reviewContext.userProblem: vactr's canvas editor engine (editor/src/code, ~12k lines) is tied to vactr types and has no plugin, widget, range/line-format or variable-height mechanism. The user wants it extracted into a standalone library emaki that vactr loads, with line-embedded plugins (video, animation), character and line formats (beat glow via marks), inline sequencer and oscilloscope plugins in vactr, a realtime GitHub-style side-by-side diff demo, and fast virtualized rendering of a 10k-line JSON file.
requiredOutcomes: emaki/ is a standalone package: cd emaki && npm ci --prefer-offline && npm run check && npm test && npm run build pass, and the boundary test proves no import escapes emaki/.

Documented public APIs: createEditor, document/transactions/history, language providers with incremental tokenization, marks (including glow), line formats, plugins, block and end-of-line widgets with DOM and animated-canvas content. Unit tests cover mapping through edits, heightmap y<->line with widgets, virtualization mount/unmount and format precedence.

Demo pages: plugin showcase, 10k-line JSON editor, and a realtime split diff (red/green line backgrounds, word marks, aligned fillers, synced scroll). A Playwright e2e drives the diff page in Chromium and WebKit.

Perf on the 10k JSON fixture in WebKit and Chromium: first paint <= 200 ms, scroll p95 <= 16.7 ms, keystroke p95 <= 16.7 ms, diff visible latency <= 100 ms; the 1k/10k/100k comparison shows per-keystroke work does not scale with document size.

vactr depends on emaki via file:../emaki. Moved engine code is gone from editor/src/code. vact syntax is an emaki language provider. Beat glow and eval flash use emaki marks. Inline sequencer and oscilloscope plugins render from live telemetry, with a persisted show/hide toggle.
vactr suites pass: editor check, vitest at or above the 2384 baseline (moved tests counted in emaki), test:style, e2e Chromium+WebKit, e2e:examples. Existing canvas perf budgets do not regress.
design-docs/specs/design-emaki.md documents architecture, API, plugin model, formatting, heightmap, diff engine, packaging and vactr integration. emaki/README.md documents usage.
nonGoals: No change to Rust sources, session protocol, scheduler, language semantics or the tree-sitter grammar (design 1).
No soft wrap, no new bidi support, no new renderer backend. The DOM renderer was already removed, so ?renderer=dom is not preserved (EM-D1, B2).
Plugins cannot write the document; the host API is read-only (design 7.2).
No inline display of bus analyzer units, which carry no source span (design 13.5).
No npm publication and no copy into tacogips/emaki in this run; the operator does that afterwards.
vim/** is not moved into emaki in this run (EM-D17).
constraints: Branch wf/emaki, one shared working directory, no git writes by workers (rule 18).

emaki imports nothing outside emaki/, has no solid-js or vactr types, and depends only on @codemirror/state 6.7.6, @codemirror/commands 6.11.1 and the pinned dev tools (rules 9, 13). vactr imports only emaki, emaki/engine, emaki/diff and emaki/json (rule 14).
Never edit test expectations, fixtures or tolerances; moved tests change only import specifiers (rule 15).

Heavy runs (editor full vitest, emaki/editor builds, Playwright, mise run build-wasm-release) take the measurement lock /Users/taco/gits/tacogips/vactr-worktrees/.measure-lock (rule 7). Rebuild wasm and editor dist before any vactr e2e (rule 8).

Scoped per-plan gates for wave siblings (rule 12b): scoped vitest is the pass gate; npm run check errors outside the plan's writePaths/sharedPaths are recorded as sibling drift; full vitest and build are informational and recorded in the plan log, not listed as plan verification. Plans alone in their wave and the single editor writer per wave keep full-suite gates.

Serial wave-join gate after each wave (rule 12a, see waveJoinGates), run by the orchestrator under the lock; the next wave starts only when the join is green; failures route to the plan owning the failing path.

Verification records use {command, exitStatus: 0, testsRun, testsPassed, failureCount: 0, outcome: "passed", log, notes}; negative controls only in mutationEvidence (rule 10), and a negative control never creates a file outside the plan's writePaths; it mutates an owned file and restores it byte-identically (amendment ca265cc). The Codex sandbox cannot run Playwright; such runs are recorded blocked-in-sandbox and run by the orchestrator (rule 11).
No audible audio (Chromium --mute-audio); never change the Mac system volume (rule 17).
UI: flat, border-radius 0, token palette, controls spaced at least 8 px, no native widget look (rule 16).
Touched or new source files stay under 1000 lines.
designDecisionsAndRationale: EM-D2: two public levels, createEditor and emaki/engine blocks; vactr composes the blocks so its surface and renderer adapters stay thin.

EM-D3: TypeScript-source exports with exact-pinned @codemirror peers; the consumer uses dedupe, inline and preserveSymlinks so file:../emaki and github:tacogips/emaki#<sha> both work with no build step. A single-instance test guards against two @codemirror/state copies.
EM-D4: sync.ts, line-bytes.ts, RevisionHistory, momentary-pointer, perf-hook, format*, syntax providers and the vact language stay in vactr.

EM-D5/EM-D6: only font weight/style reshape; color/opacity re-tint; background, glow, underline and strike are quads. Glow is three expanded quads after mark backgrounds with no shader change, so audio-rate beat glow stays cheap.
EM-D7: decoration precedence reproduces today's draw order (gpu.test.ts first four draws unchanged).

EM-D8: sparse heightmap with prefix sums, O(log w) lookup and O(1) with no widgets; renderer text slot y, visible rows and animated rect tops go through it, and heightmap.revision is in viewportKey (repair of EMK-R5-01).
EM-D9: line-kind language providers with checkpoints every 32 lines; vact stays a span-kind provider.
EM-D10: beat glow and eval flash are an animated-mark plugin; PLAYING_MARK adds glow over today's color.

EM-D11/EM-D12: emaki scripts use Playwright request routing instead of a localhost server; keystroke and scroll gates measure editor work per frame plus next-frame presentation, with raw keydown-to-present recorded.
EM-D13: the sequencer anchor is the lowest src span per slot, placed below the last line of its containing top-level form.
EM-D14: canvas budgets keep the repository gates; 4 ms text-dirty is a recorded target, not a gate.
EM-D15/EM-D16: moved tests keep their counts (vactr + emaki >= 2384 + new tests); inline widgets default on under vactr.inlineWidgets.

EM-D17/EM-D18/EM-D19: vim/** stays in vactr behind a generic ModalKeyHook; the keyboard fallbackShortcut tri-state preserves stop-all vs cut; the drag-gesture expando becomes markDragGesture/isDragGesture.
Six serial waves on one branch with wave-join gates (repair of EMK-R5-02), because the shared working directory cannot isolate sibling half-written files.

Per-plan full-suite results in parallel waves are informational; the authoritative package-wide result is the serial wave-join gate.

executionModel: Six waves on one branch and one working directory. W1: EMK-CORE runs alone. It creates the package and pins the shared contract types, so it is the root of the DAG. W2: EMK-DECOR, EMK-WIDGETS, EMK-LANG and EMK-DIFF run in parallel with disjoint writePaths. W3: EMK-API and EMK-VAC-SWITCH run in parallel. EMK-VAC-SWITCH may edit the listed emaki engine sharedPaths only for parity defects that unchanged vactr tests expose; EMK-API does not edit those files. W4: EMK-DIFF-DEMO, EMK-JSON-DEMO, EMK-SHOWCASE and EMK-VAC-PLUGINS run in parallel. W5: EMK-PERF runs alone, with perf-repair sharedPaths. W6: EMK-CLOSEOUT runs alone and runs all gates G1-G10 on the combined tree. Heavy runs (full vitest in editor, any Playwright, emaki and editor builds, mise run build-wasm-release) take the measurement lock at /Users/taco/gits/tacogips/vactr-worktrees/.measure-lock. The lock serializes these runs but does not isolate a sibling's half-written files, so plans that share a wave are judged only on scoped gates (rule 12b). After every wave the orchestrator runs a serial wave-join gate (rule 12a: emaki check, full vitest and build; editor check from wave 3; editor full vitest at wave 3; diff e2e (G4), smoke and the dist page checks at wave 4) under the lock, with logs in tmp/emaki/wave-<n>-join/. Failures are routed by failing file path, and the next wave starts only when the join is green. Evidence goes under tmp/emaki/<planId>/ and is never in writePaths. Workers edit only their own plan file's Progress Log. The design and all plans are committed before native fanout starts.
